## Multipass for local testing

Multipass runs Ubuntu virtual machines (VMs) on your own computer. Use a
VM to test a cloud-init file and a deploy before you create a real
server. A VM costs nothing and takes a few minutes to start. Install
Multipass and put the `multipass` command on your PATH.

[`Multipass`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multipass)
wraps the `multipass` command. `launch` starts a VM. It takes an
optional cloud-init file from
[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init)
or
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init),
and optional host folders to mount in the VM as
`mounts={host_path: vm_path}`. `vms` lists the VM names. `ip` returns
the address of a VM. `exec_` runs a command inside a VM. `rm` deletes a
VM. Any other `multipass` subcommand works as a method. For example,
`mp.info('testvm')` runs `multipass info testvm`. The module creates one
instance, `mp`.

[`deploy_mp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy_mp)
is [`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy)
for a VM. It creates the target directory if it is missing and gives it
to the
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) user.
Then it copies your app in and starts it. The cell below lists the VMs
on the machine that built these docs. That machine had none.

## Cloud-init generation

A new cloud server starts as a bare Ubuntu image. Cloud-init is a
program that runs on the first boot of the server. It reads a YAML file
supplied when the server is created. It installs packages, creates
users, adds SSH keys and runs commands.
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
and
[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init)
write that file. Each returns an `AttrDict` with the YAML text as `yaml`
and the path of the matching private key as `key`.

[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
is for a public server on Hetzner or Lightsail. It builds the file with
`cloud_init_config` from fastcloudinit. That function turns on the UFW
firewall with only SSH allowed, adds log rotation and reboots at the
end.
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
adds the `fail2ban` and `unattended-upgrades` packages. Unless you pass
`docker=False`, it also installs Docker and adds the user to the
`docker` group. Other keyword arguments go to `cloud_init_config`.

[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init)
is for a Multipass VM. It uses the smaller `cloud_init_base`. The user
and Docker setup are the same as in
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init).
[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init)
sets no firewall, installs no `fail2ban` and adds no swap file. It
reboots only when there are commands to run. The Docker install counts
as commands.

Both functions create one user,
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) by
default. The user can run `sudo` without a password. The user logs in
only with the SSH keys in `pub_keys`. If you omit `pub_keys`,
[`gen_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#gen_key)
uses the ed25519 key pair at `~/.ssh/<hostname>`. It makes the key pair
when no private key is there. It reuses a private key that is already
there and writes a missing `.pub` file from it.
`gen_key(hostname, replace=True)` makes a new key pair. `key` is the
path of the private key. If you pass `pub_keys`, `key` is None. Use
`pkgs` for extra packages and `cmds` for extra shell commands. The
commands run after the Docker install.

[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
also adds a swap file and sets the kernel swappiness to 10. The swap
file is 4 GB by default. A swappiness of 10 makes the server swap only
under real memory pressure. Without swap, a small server that runs
several containers kills a process when memory runs out. Pass
`swap=None` to skip swap, or a size such as `swap='2G'`. Pass
`swappiness` to change the value. The commands add the swap file only if
`/swapfile` does not exist, and they run before the Docker install.
[`swap_cmds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#swap_cmds)
returns the commands on their own, for a server that already exists.

The first test below passes a key, so
[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init)
generates none. The second test generates a key pair and deletes it.

### multi_init

``` python
def multi_init(
    hostname, pub_keys:NoneType=None, username:str='deploy', docker:bool=True, pkgs:NoneType=None,
    cmds:NoneType=None,
    key_dir:NoneType=None, # folder for the generated key pair when `pub_keys` is None; default `~/.ssh`
):
```

*Write a cloud-init file for a local Multipass VM, generating a key pair
if `pub_keys` is None.*

``` python
ci = multi_init('mylocal', 'ssh-rsa AAAA...')
assert '#cloud-config' in ci.yaml and 'get.docker.com' in ci.yaml and 'ufw' not in ci.yaml
assert 'power_state' in ci.yaml and ci.key is None
print(ci.yaml)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as kd:
    ci2 = multi_init('mylocal', docker=False, key_dir=kd)
    assert 'get.docker.com' not in ci2.yaml and 'power_state' not in ci2.yaml
    assert ci2.key == Path(kd)/'mylocal' and ci2.key.exists()
    assert Path(str(ci2.key) + '.pub').exists()
    k1 = gen_key('mylocal', kd)
    other = gen_key('other', kd)
    k1.pub.write_text(other.pub_str[0] + '\n')
    k2 = gen_key('mylocal', kd)
    assert k2.pub_str == k1.pub_str != other.pub_str and k1.pub.read_text().strip() == k1.pub_str[0]
    k3 = gen_key('mylocal', kd, replace=True)
    assert k3.pub_str != k1.pub_str
print('multi_init OK')
```

## Hetzner

[`Hetzner`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner)
manages servers on Hetzner Cloud through the hcloud Python SDK, so you
do not need Hetzner’s command-line tool or a config file. It reads the
API token from `HCLOUD_TOKEN` unless you pass `token=`, and raises
`ValueError` if there is none.

`create` makes a server and returns its IP address, name, key path and
the raw SDK response. Give it the result of
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
as `cloud_init`, and the key path comes back with the server. `ssh_keys`
is a different way to log in. It names keys stored in your Hetzner
account, and Hetzner adds them to the root user only. They give no
access to the
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) user
that cloud-init creates, so `create` refuses to take both. `key_names`
lists the stored keys for that purpose.

`servers` lists your servers with their IP and status, `get` returns one
by name or None, `server_ip` returns its address and `delete` removes
it. Deleting a server that does not exist does nothing.

## Lightsail

Lightsail is the fixed-price virtual private server (VPS) service of
Amazon.
[`Lightsail`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#lightsail)
has the same methods as
[`Hetzner`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner):
`servers`, `get`, `server_ip`, `create` and `delete`. It talks to AWS
through boto3.
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
works with either class. boto3 is an optional extra:
`pip install 'vpseasy[aws]'`. Without boto3,
[`Lightsail()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#lightsail)
raises `ImportError`. Credentials come from the standard AWS chain. For
example, name an SSO profile in `AWS_PROFILE` or pass `profile=`. The
region defaults to `ap-southeast-2` (Sydney).

`create` is safe to run twice. It does not create an instance that
already exists. In both cases it calls `server_ip`, which waits until
the instance is running. `server_ip` raises `TimeoutError` after `tout`
seconds (300 by default). If `static_ip` is True, the default, `create`
then attaches a static IP address named `<name>-ip`. A static IP that is
already allocated is reused. If `ports` is not None, `create` sets the
open public ports to `ports`. If `snapshots` is set, `create` turns on a
daily automatic snapshot at that time. By default only SSH (port 22) is
open, because web traffic arrives through the Cloudflare tunnel. The
default snapshot time is 16:00 UTC. `delete` removes the instance.
Unless you pass `release_ip=False`, it also releases the static IP.
`bucket` makes a storage bucket for backups. The Litestream section
covers it.

Lightsail runs user data as a shell script. It does not read
cloud-config YAML. When the user data starts with `#cloud-config`,
`create` converts it with
[`cloud_init_sh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#cloud_init_sh).
Other user data passes through unchanged. The script runs these steps in
order: it sets the hostname, turns off password logins, creates the
users with their groups, sudo rules and SSH keys, writes files, applies
apt settings, installs packages and runs the commands. It turns off
password logins only when the YAML sets `ssh_pwauth: false`. The script
does not reboot. It keeps the original YAML in
`/var/lib/vpseasy/cloud-config.yaml` and logs to
`/var/log/vpseasy-init.log`. When it finishes, it creates
`/var/lib/vpseasy/ready`. If a step failed, it creates
`/var/lib/vpseasy/error` instead.
[`chk_cloud_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#chk_cloud_init)
reads those files.

[`cloud_init_sh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#cloud_init_sh)
converts these top-level keys: `hostname`, `users`, `write_files`,
`apt`, `packages`, `runcmd`, `package_update`, `package_upgrade` and
`ssh_pwauth`. It ignores `preserve_hostname`, `disable_root` and
`power_state`. It raises `ValueError` for any other top-level key, for a
user key it cannot convert, and for an invalid `write_files` permission.
The conversion exists because cloud-init did not create the users on
Ubuntu 24.04 when it ran on YAML placed in `/etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d`.

*Create, list and delete AWS Lightsail instances through boto3, using
the standard AWS credentials.*

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
y = vps_init('lh', 'ssh-ed25519 AAAATEST lh').yaml
ud = cloud_init_sh(y)
subprocess.run(['bash', '-n'], input=ud, text=True, check=True)
assert ud.startswith('#!/bin/bash\n') and y.rstrip() in ud
assert "useradd -m -s /bin/bash deploy" in ud and 'ssh-ed25519 AAAATEST lh' in ud and 'deploy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' in ud
assert 'get.docker.com' in ud and 'ufw --force enable' in ud and ud.rstrip().endswith('touch /var/lib/vpseasy/ready')
assert '--force-confold' in ud and 'PasswordAuthentication no' in ud and 'rm -f /var/lib/vpseasy/error' in ud
body = ud[ud.index('hostnamectl'):]
assert body.index('useradd') < body.index('apt-get') < body.index('get.docker.com')
test_fail(lambda: cloud_init_sh('#cloud-config\nbootcmd: [echo hi]\n'), contains='bootcmd')
u = cloud_init_sh("#cloud-config\nusers: [default, {name: bob, groups: 'sudo, docker'}]\n")
assert 'usermod -aG sudo,docker bob' in u and 'default' not in u.split('VPSEASY_EOF')[-1]
test_fail(lambda: cloud_init_sh('#cloud-config\nusers: [{name: bob, lock_passwd: true}]\n'), contains='lock_passwd')
w = cloud_init_sh("#cloud-config\nwrite_files: [{path: /etc/x, content: hi, permissions: 0600, owner: 'a b'}]\n")
assert 'chmod 600 /etc/x' in w and "chown 'a b' /etc/x" in w
test_fail(lambda: cloud_init_sh("#cloud-config\nwrite_files: [{path: /etc/x, permissions: '0644; rm -rf /'}]\n"), contains='permissions')
```

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
from botocore.stub import Stubber
ls = Lightsail(region='ap-southeast-2')
st = Stubber(ls._c)
def inst(state='running', ip='3.1.2.3'): return {'instance': {'name': 'lh', 'state': {'name': state}, **({'publicIpAddress': ip} if ip else {})}}

st.add_response('get_instances', {'instances': [inst()['instance']]})
with st: test_eq(ls.servers(), [dict(name='lh', ip='3.1.2.3', status='running')])

st.add_response('get_instance', inst('pending', None), {'instanceName': 'lh'})
st.add_response('get_instance', inst(), {'instanceName': 'lh'})
with st: test_eq(ls.server_ip('lh', interval=0), '3.1.2.3')

st.add_response('get_instance', inst(), {'instanceName': 'lh'})
st.add_response('get_instance', inst(), {'instanceName': 'lh'})
with st: r = ls.create('lh', cloud_init='#cloud-config\n', static_ip=False, ports=None, snapshots=None)
test_eq(r.ip, '3.1.2.3')

st.add_client_error('get_instance', service_error_code='NotFoundException', expected_params={'instanceName': 'nope'})
with st: test_eq(ls.get('nope'), None)
st.assert_no_pending_responses()
```

``` python
st.assert_no_pending_responses()
```

## SSH helpers

These functions call the system `ssh` and `rsync` commands. No Python
SSH library is needed. They share these arguments. `user` (or `u`) is
the login name,
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) by
default. The private key comes from the first of these that applies: the
path in `key` (or `k`); then `~/.ssh/<name>` if you pass `name`; then
the key that `ssh` picks by itself. If you pass `name` and the file
`~/.ssh/<name>` does not exist, the function raises `FileNotFoundError`.
`key_pass` is the passphrase of an encrypted key. `password` is a login
password for servers that accept one. Pass `True` to either to be asked
for it. Every function that connects takes `port`, the SSH port, which
is 22 by default. The first connection to a new host adds it to
`known_hosts` without asking.

[`run_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#run_ssh)
runs one or more commands on the host, joined with `&&`. It returns
their output. If the commands wrote to stderr,
[`run_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#run_ssh)
appends that text after `;;`. If a command fails,
[`run_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#run_ssh)
raises `IOError`. With `check=False` it returns `(exit code, output)`
instead. `stdin_data` is sent to the remote command’s standard input.

[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) copies a
local directory to `path` on the host with rsync. If `path` is missing
or not writable,
[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) first
creates it with `sudo` and gives it to `user`.
[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) deletes
remote files that are not in `src`. Point it at a directory that belongs
to the app alone. `exclude` skips files that match a pattern. `include`
copies only the files that match a pattern. A pattern that ends in `/`
takes a whole directory. `extra` adds rsync flags such as `--checksum`.

[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) raises
`CalledProcessError` when rsync fails. Nothing runs on a half-copied
folder. [`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync)
returns the rsync exit code. With `check=False`, a failed rsync returns
its exit code instead of raising.

[`sync_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync_paths)
copies chosen paths instead of a whole folder. Use it for content that
changes without a rebuild, such as the files behind a bind mount. Each
path under `src` goes to the same path under `path`.
[`sync_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync_paths)
runs one rsync per path. `--delete` removes only files inside that path.
It never reaches the rest of the folder on the server. A path that is
missing from `src` is skipped. rsync’s `--mkpath` creates missing remote
folders. `delete=False`, `mkpath=False` and `itemize=False` turn off the
matching rsync flags.

`last` names a pattern. rsync holds the files that match it back from a
first pass and sends them in a second pass. Use `last` when something on
the server watches for one kind of file. With `last='*.json'`, an audio
file is in place before the JSON file that names it.

A path that names the folder itself raises `ValueError`. Examples are
`.`, `''` and `/`. A path that resolves to the folder, or leaves it
through `..` or a symlink, also raises `ValueError`. Its `--delete`
would reach the whole folder.

`dry_run=True` lists the changes without making them. With `host=None`,
the copy goes to a local folder.
[`sync_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync_paths)
returns the rsync commands it ran.
[`rsync_cmds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rsync_cmds)
returns the commands without running them. It raises the same
`ValueError`.

[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) runs
[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync). Then it
runs `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans` in `path`. It adds
`--build` unless you pass `build=False`. It starts Compose only if
Docker works for the user and `path` holds a `docker-compose.yml`.
Otherwise it stops after the copy.
[`chk_docker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#chk_docker)
is the Docker check on its own. It returns True or False. After a build,
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) keeps
the new image and the image it replaced with
[`keep_image`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#keep_image).
[`rollback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rollback)
can then return to either image. `keep=0` turns this off. After the
build, `prune=True` deletes dangling images and the build cache. Without
pruning, they grow by the size of an image on every deploy. Pruning
leaves kept images, because they carry tags.

[`ssh_cmd`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#ssh_cmd),
[`res_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#res_key) and
[`askpass_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#askpass_env)
are the functions the others share.
[`ssh_cmd`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#ssh_cmd)
returns the `ssh` command line.
[`res_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#res_key)
looks up the key.
[`askpass_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#askpass_env)
is a context manager that answers a password prompt. They are public for
callers that run their own `ssh` or `rsync`. `_ssh`, `_res_key` and
`_askpass_env` remain as aliases.

[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) quotes
the remote path and the key path, so a space in either stays inside one
shell word. The cell records the commands with a stand-in for
`subprocess.run` and shows the remote command.

``` python
def _fake(cmd, *a, **k): _rec.append(cmd); return _sp.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, b'', b'')
_rec = []
with patch.object(subprocess, 'run', _fake): sync('h', '.', path='/srv/my app', key='/k/my key')
_mk, _rs = _rec
assert '/srv/my app' in shlex.split(_mk[-1])
assert '/k/my key' in shlex.split(_rs[_rs.index('-e')+1])
_mk[-1]
```

[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) protects
Compose bind sources inside the remote deploy root from deletion. Local
files in those bind sources still transfer. A bind source that names the
whole deploy root raises `ValueError`.
[`sync_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync_paths)
applies the same protection within each selected path. Both functions
read the local Compose file. Named volumes stored by Docker and bind
sources outside the deploy root need no rsync protection. Add other
paths with `exclude`. Keep the local Compose file available when
syncing. Compose variable interpolation and override files, including
automatic override files, are not resolved. Add their bind sources with
`exclude`.

[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy)
removes dangling images and prunes build cache older than 168 hours
after a successful deploy. Set `prune=False` to skip pruning. The
default protects recent build cache while limiting old cache growth.

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    root = Path(td)
    (root/'nested').mkdir()
    (root/'data').mkdir()
    (root/'docker-compose.yml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump(dict(services=dict(app=dict(volumes=[
        './data:/app/data', './nested/backups:/app/backups',
        dict(type='bind', source='/srv/app/archive', target='/archive'), './settings.json:/settings.json',
        'named:/named'])))))
    _rec = []
    with patch.object(subprocess, 'run', _fake): sync('h', root, exclude=['extra'])
    cmd = _rec[-1]
    rules = [cmd[i+1] for i, v in enumerate(cmd) if v == '--filter']
    assert all('P ' + p in rules for p in ['/data', '/nested/backups', '/archive', '/settings.json']), rules
    assert cmd[cmd.index('--exclude')+1] == 'extra'
    cmds = rsync_cmds(['nested/', 'data/'], root, 'deploy@h:/srv/app')
    assert len(cmds) == 2, cmds
    assert 'P /backups' in cmds[0], cmds
    assert 'P /***' in cmds[1], cmds
    (root/'docker-compose.yml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump(dict(services=dict(app=dict(volumes=['.:/app'])))))
    with patch.object(subprocess, 'run', _fake):
        test_fail(lambda: sync('h', root), contains='whole deploy root')
rules
```

``` python
_prune_calls = []
with patch.dict(deploy.__globals__, sync=lambda *a, **kw: None,
                chk_docker=lambda **kw: True, _chk_compose=lambda **kw: True,
                _img=lambda *a: 'app',
                run_ssh=lambda host, cmd, **kw: _prune_calls.append(cmd) or ''):
    deploy('h', build=False, keep=0)
    assert any('docker builder prune -f --filter until=168h' in c for c in _prune_calls), _prune_calls
    _prune_calls.clear()
    deploy('h', build=False, keep=0, prune=False)
    assert not any('prune' in c for c in _prune_calls)
_prune_calls
```

## Verification helpers

`create` returns as soon as the provider accepts the request, while the
server is still booting and cloud-init is still working. Copying files
at that point fails or races the setup, so these functions wait.

[`wait_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ssh)
tries a trivial SSH command every `interval` seconds until it succeeds,
and raises `TimeoutError` after `tout` seconds.
[`chk_cloud_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#chk_cloud_init)
asks once whether setup has finished and returns `done`, `running` or
`error`. On a server set up by a
[`cloud_init_sh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#cloud_init_sh)
script it reads that script’s marker files in `/var/lib/vpseasy`.
Elsewhere it checks for `/var/lib/cloud/instance/boot-finished`, the
file cloud-init writes when it is done. It returns `unknown` if the
command printed nothing.
[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready),
further down, runs both in a loop.

    wait_ssh: tout=0 → TimeoutError OK

[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready)
waits for SSH with
[`wait_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ssh).
[`wait_ssh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ssh)
retries every `interval` seconds and raises `TimeoutError` after `tout`
seconds. Then
[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready)
calls
[`chk_cloud_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#chk_cloud_init)
every `interval` seconds until it returns `done`.
[`chk_cloud_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#chk_cloud_init)
returns `done`, `running` or `error`.
[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready)
raises `RuntimeError` when the status is `error`. A slow server gets
`retries` extra rounds of `tout` seconds each.
[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready)
prints a message before each extra round. After the last round it raises
`TimeoutError`.

[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
is the function most people want. It takes a server name, a local
directory and a provider such as
[`Hetzner()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner)
or
[`Lightsail()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#lightsail).
If the provider has no server with that name,
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
creates one from `vps_init(name)`. That call makes a new key pair at
`~/.ssh/<name>`.
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
then removes any old `known_hosts` entry for the new IP address. If the
server exists,
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
uses the key at `~/.ssh/<name>`, or `key` if you pass one. In both cases
it then runs
[`wait_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_ready)
and [`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy).
It returns an `AttrDict` with the IP address as `ip`, the server name as
`name` and the key path as `key`. Extra keyword arguments go to the
`create` method of the provider. Examples are `server_type=` for Hetzner
and `bundle=` for Lightsail. For an existing server,
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
does not call `create`, and these arguments have no effect.
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
checks for the server before it creates one. Running it again redeploys
to the same server.

[`hetzner_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner_deploy)
is
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
with a
[`Hetzner`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner)
provider. It takes the Hetzner arguments `image`, `server_type` and
`location`. `hz` is an existing
[`Hetzner`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner)
client.
[`hetzner_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#hetzner_deploy)
remains for code written before Lightsail support.

The tests after these two functions use a fake provider. They check both
paths without touching a real server.

``` python
def vps_deploy(
    name, # server name, also the key file name under ~/.ssh when `key` is not given
    src, # local path to sync and deploy
    provider, # Hetzner(), Lightsail() or anything with get, server_ip and create
    user:str='deploy', # login user on the server; also the user a new server's cloud-init creates
    key:NoneType=None, # path of the SSH private key, whose `.pub` file a new server authorizes; overrides the lookup of `~/.ssh/<name>`
    path:str='/srv/app', # remote path to sync to and deploy at
    build:bool=True, # pass `--build` to `docker compose up` when True
    include:NoneType=None, # rsync include (whitelist) patterns
    exclude:NoneType=None, # rsync exclude (blacklist) patterns
    extra:NoneType=None, # extra rsync flags passed to `sync`, such as '--checksum' or ['--ignore-times','--partial']
    key_pass:NoneType=None, # passphrase of an encrypted SSH key; True asks for it
    password:NoneType=None, # login password of the server; True asks for it
    tout:int=600, # seconds to wait for SSH, and for each round of cloud-init polling
    retries:int=2, # extra rounds of cloud-init polling before raising TimeoutError
    verbose:bool=True, # print progress while waiting and deploying
    port:int=22, # SSH port on the server
    prune:bool=True, # delete dangling images and build cache older than 168 hours after deploy
    keep:int=3, # timestamped images of the app kept for `rollback`; 0 keeps none
    svc:str='app', # the Compose service whose image is kept
    img:NoneType=None, # that image's name when the Compose project is not named after `path`
    **create_kw
):
```

*Create server `name` on `provider` if it does not exist, wait for its
setup, deploy `src`, and return its ip, name and key.*

``` python
@contextmanager
def patch_to_fakes(calls):
    'Replace `wait_ready`, `deploy`, `vps_init` and `subprocess` with fakes where `vps_deploy` resolves them. No key or `known_hosts` file is touched.'
    g = vps_deploy.__globals__
    ks = 'wait_ready', 'deploy', 'vps_init', 'subprocess'
    o = {k: g[k] for k in ks}
    g['wait_ready'] = lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('wait_ready', a, k))
    g['deploy'] = lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('deploy', a, k))
    g['vps_init'] = lambda name, *a, **k: AttrDict(yaml='#cloud-config\n', key='/tmp/k')
    g['subprocess'] = AttrDict(run=lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('ssh-keygen', a, k)))
    try: yield
    finally: g.update(o)

class FakeProvider:
    def __init__(self, made=()): self.made, self.kw = list(made), None
    def get(self, name): return {'name': name} if name in self.made else None
    def server_ip(self, name): return '192.0.2.9'
    def create(self, name, cloud_init=None, **kw): self.made.append(name); self.kw = kw; return AttrDict(ip='192.0.2.9', name=name, key='/tmp/k')

calls, fp = [], FakeProvider()
with patch_to_fakes(calls): r = vps_deploy('svc', '.', fp, verbose=False, bundle='nano_3_0')
test_eq(r, AttrDict(ip='192.0.2.9', name='svc', key='/tmp/k'))
test_eq([c[0] for c in calls], ['ssh-keygen', 'wait_ready', 'deploy'])
test_eq(fp.kw, dict(bundle='nano_3_0'))

calls, fp = [], FakeProvider(made=['svc'])
with patch_to_fakes(calls): r = vps_deploy('svc', '.', fp, key='/tmp/other', verbose=False)
test_eq(r, AttrDict(ip='192.0.2.9', name='svc', key='/tmp/other'))
test_eq(fp.kw, None)

calls, fp = [], FakeProvider(made=['svc'])
with patch_to_fakes(calls): vps_deploy('svc', '.', fp, key='/tmp/other', verbose=False, port=2222, keep=5, prune=False)
test_eq((calls[0][2]['port'], calls[1][2]['port'], calls[1][2]['keep'], calls[1][2]['prune']), (2222, 2222, 5, False))
```

## Rollback

A deploy builds a new image and replaces the running container. A bad
build takes the site down.
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) keeps
the image that it replaces.
[`rollback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rollback)
starts that image again.

Compose names the image that it builds for a service after the project
folder and the service. The folder `/srv/app` with the service `app`
builds `app-app:latest`. Compose removes characters other than
lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_` from the folder name. vpseasy
does the same, and it also drops a leading `-` or `_`. Pass `img` when
the project has another name, set by `name:` in the Compose file or by
`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`.
[`vps_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_deploy)
passes `img` on to
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy).

After each build,
[`keep_image`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#keep_image)
tags the new image with its build time in UTC, such as
`app-app:20261019T063000`. It tags the image that ran before as
`app-app:prev`. It also gives that image its build time when the image
has none. Then it deletes the timestamped tags past the newest `keep` by
build time. `keep` is three by default. It never deletes the tags of the
running image and of `prev`. An image with two timestamps counts once. A
build whose second another build already holds takes the next free
second.
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) runs
[`keep_image`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#keep_image)
even when the restart after the build fails. The new build already holds
`latest`. A build keeps its tag until it falls out of the newest `keep`,
whatever rollbacks happen in between.

A failed `docker rmi` leaves the tag in place. This happens when a
stopped container still uses the tag. The deploy continues. Pruning
after the build deletes only dangling images and the build cache. Tagged
images stay.
[`kept_images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#kept_images)
lists the kept tags, newest first, with their image IDs.

[`rollback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rollback)
points the service at a kept image and restarts it. Without `to`, it
picks the newest kept image that is older than the running one. Calling
it twice goes back two builds. With `to`, it uses that tag, which is a
timestamp or `prev`.
[`rollback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rollback)
raises `ValueError` when no kept image is older than the running one. It
also raises `ValueError` when the tag `to` is not on the server.

Before it switches,
[`rollback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#rollback)
tags the running image `prev`. `prev` always names the image that ran
before the current one. `rollback(host, 'prev')` undoes the last deploy
or rollback. A rollback moves only the tags `latest` and `prev`. The
running image keeps its timestamp. `rollback(host, to=<its tag>)`
returns to it after any number of rollbacks. vpseasy 0.0.25 and earlier
tagged the replaced image `undo`. vpseasy no longer writes or reads that
tag. The restart is `docker compose up -d --no-build --force-recreate`
for the one service. Compose uses the retagged image and does not build.

A rollback restores the image and nothing else. Files that
[`sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#sync) copied to
the server stay as the last deploy left them. Examples are the Compose
file, the Caddyfile and bind-mounted folders. Volumes and databases also
stay as they were. The next
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy)
builds from your source again. It keeps the rolled-back image like any
other.

### kept_images

``` python
def kept_images(
    host, path:str='/srv/app', svc:str='app', img:NoneType=None, **kw
)->list:
```

*Return the timestamped images kept of `svc` on `host`, as (tag, image

``` python
class FakeDocker:
    'A fake server. The commands that `run_ssh` sends read and change a table of images, their build times and their tags.'
    def __init__(self, tags=None):
        self.tags, self.cmds, self.kw, self.n = dict(tags or {}), [], [], 0
        self.imgs = {i: '' for i in self.tags.values()}
    def __call__(self, host, *cmds, **kw):
        self.kw.append(kw); out = []
        for c in cmds:
            self.cmds.append(c); w = c.replace("'", '').split()
            if c.startswith('docker image inspect'):
                i = self.tags.get(w[5], w[5] if w[5] in self.imgs else '')
                out.append(self.imgs.get(i, '') if 'Created' in w[4] else i)
            elif c.startswith('docker image ls'): out += [f'{t.split(":")[1]} {i}' for t, i in self.tags.items() if t.split(':')[0] == w[3]]
            elif c.startswith('docker image prune'): self.imgs = {i: t for i, t in self.imgs.items() if i in self.tags.values()}
            elif c.startswith('docker tag'): self.tags[w[3]] = self.tags.get(w[2], w[2])
            elif c.startswith('docker rmi'): [self.tags.pop(t) for t in w[2:] if ':' in t]
            elif c.startswith('ls '): out.append(w[1])
            elif '--build' in c:
                self.n += 1; i = self.tags['app-app:latest'] = f'sha256:new{self.n}'
                self.imgs[i] = f'2026-10-{10+self.n:02d}T00:00:00.123456789Z'
        return '\n'.join(out)

@contextmanager
def fake_server(fd, ts):
    'Send `run_ssh` and `sync` to `fd`, and make `time.strftime` return the stamps in `ts` in turn.'
    g = rollback.__globals__; o = {k: g[k] for k in ('run_ssh', 'sync')}
    g['run_ssh'], g['sync'] = fd, lambda *a, **k: 0
    try:
        with patch('time.strftime', side_effect=ts): yield
    finally: g.update(o)

fd = FakeDocker()
ts = [f'2026101{i}T000000' for i in range(10)]
with fake_server(fd, ts):
    deploy('h', key='/k', port=2222)
    test_eq(fd.tags, {'app-app:latest': 'sha256:new1', 'app-app:20261011T000000': 'sha256:new1'})
    for _ in range(4): deploy('h', key='/k', port=2222)
    assert all(k['port'] == 2222 for k in fd.kw)
    test_eq(kept_images('h'), [('20261015T000000', 'sha256:new5'), ('20261014T000000', 'sha256:new4'), ('20261013T000000', 'sha256:new3')])
    test_eq(fd.tags['app-app:prev'], 'sha256:new4')
    assert any(c.startswith('docker image prune -f') for c in fd.cmds)
    test_eq(rollback('h', verbose=False), '20261014T000000')
    test_eq((fd.tags['app-app:latest'], fd.tags['app-app:prev']), ('sha256:new4', 'sha256:new5'))
    assert fd.cmds[-1] == 'cd /srv/app && docker compose up -d --no-build --force-recreate app'
    test_eq(rollback('h', verbose=False), '20261013T000000')
    test_eq(rollback('h', to='20261015T000000', verbose=False), '20261015T000000')
    test_fail(lambda: rollback('h', to='20250101T000000', verbose=False), contains='not on h')
    deploy('h', keep=0, prune=False)
    test_eq(len(kept_images('h')), 3)

fd = FakeDocker({'web-site:latest': 'sha256:a', 'web-site:20261001T000000': 'sha256:a'})
with fake_server(fd, ts):
    test_fail(lambda: rollback('h', path='/srv/web', svc='site', verbose=False), contains='no kept image')
    test_eq(keep_image('h', '/srv/web', 'site'), '20261001T000000')
    test_eq(_img('/srv/My.App', 'app', None), 'myapp-app')
    test_eq(_img('/srv/_web', 'app', None), 'web-app')
fd = FakeDocker({'app-app:latest': 'sha256:b', 'app-app:20261001T000000': 'sha256:a'})   # a running image from before 0.0.26 has no timestamp
_fd = lambda host, *c, **kw: fd(host, *c, **kw) + ' ;; Warning: Permanently added 1.2.3.4'   # ssh's stderr on a first connection
with fake_server(_fd, ['20261002T000000']):
    test_eq(rollback('h', verbose=False), '20261001T000000')
    test_eq((fd.tags['app-app:latest'], fd.tags['app-app:prev'], fd.tags['app-app:20261002T000000']), ('sha256:a', 'sha256:b', 'sha256:b'))
print('keep_image and rollback OK')
```

``` python
fd = FakeDocker()
def reachable(keep=3):
    'Every tagged image exists, and so do the newest `keep` builds, `latest` and `prev`.'
    built = sorted(fd.imgs.values(), reverse=True)
    newest = {f'sha256:new{n}' for n in range(max(fd.n - keep, 0) + 1, fd.n + 1)}
    assert set(fd.tags.values()) <= set(fd.imgs), (fd.tags, fd.imgs)
    assert newest <= set(fd.imgs), (newest, fd.imgs)
    assert all(i in {i for t, i in kept_images('h')} for i in newest), (newest, fd.tags)
cur = lambda: (fd.tags['app-app:latest'], fd.tags.get('app-app:prev'))
with fake_server(fd, ts):
    for _ in range(3): deploy('h'); reachable()
    test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new3', 'sha256:new2'))
    test_eq(kept_images('h'), [('20261013T000000', 'sha256:new3'), ('20261012T000000', 'sha256:new2'), ('20261011T000000', 'sha256:new1')])
    test_eq(rollback('h', verbose=False), '20261012T000000'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new2', 'sha256:new3'))
    test_eq(rollback('h', verbose=False), '20261011T000000'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new1', 'sha256:new2'))
    test_fail(lambda: rollback('h', verbose=False), contains='no kept image')
    test_eq(rollback('h', 'prev', verbose=False), 'prev'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new2', 'sha256:new1'))
    test_eq(rollback('h', 'prev', verbose=False), 'prev'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new1', 'sha256:new2'))
    test_eq(rollback('h', '20261013T000000', verbose=False), '20261013T000000'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new3', 'sha256:new1'))
    deploy('h'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new4', 'sha256:new3'))
    test_eq(set(fd.imgs), {f'sha256:new{n}' for n in range(2, 5)})   # new1 fell out of the newest three and was neither latest nor prev
    rollback('h', '20261012T000000', verbose=False); deploy('h'); reachable(); test_eq(cur(), ('sha256:new5', 'sha256:new2'))
    test_eq(set(fd.imgs), {'sha256:new2', 'sha256:new3', 'sha256:new4', 'sha256:new5'})   # new2 stays as prev past the newest three
fd = FakeDocker({'app-app:latest': 'sha256:a'}); fd.imgs['sha256:a'] = '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z'   # a build whose restart fails still gets its tag, and the one before it `prev`
def _fail(host, *c, **kw):
    r = fd(host, *c, **kw)
    if any('--build' in x for x in c): raise IOError('port is already allocated')
    return r
with fake_server(_fail, ts):
    test_fail(lambda: deploy('h'), contains='port is already allocated')
    test_eq((cur(), sorted(t for t in fd.tags if t[8:9].isdigit())), (('sha256:new1', 'sha256:a'), ['app-app:20261001T000000', 'app-app:20261011T000000']))
fd = FakeDocker()   # builds sharing a second (reproducible builds) get distinct tags
_c = FakeDocker.__call__
def _same(host, *c, **kw):
    r = _c(fd, host, *c, **kw)
    for i in fd.imgs: fd.imgs[i] = '1980-01-01T00:00:00Z'
    return r
with fake_server(_same, ts):
    for _ in range(4): deploy('h'); reachable()
    test_eq([t for t, _ in kept_images('h')], ['19800101T000003', '19800101T000002', '19800101T000001'])
fd = FakeDocker({'app-app:latest': 'sha256:c', 'app-app:20261003T000000': 'sha256:c', 'app-app:20261002T000000': 'sha256:b', 'app-app:20261001T000000': 'sha256:b', 'app-app:20260930T000000': 'sha256:a'})
with fake_server(fd, ts): keep_image('h', keep=3)
test_eq(set(fd.tags.values()), {'sha256:a', 'sha256:b', 'sha256:c'})   # an image tagged twice takes one of the three places
print('rollback sequences OK')
```

## After a deploy

[`wait_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_http)
requests `url` until it answers 200. It tries up to `tries` times,
`poll` seconds apart. Each request times out after `timeout` seconds. It
returns True when the URL answers 200 and False when the tries run out.
Use it after
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) and
before anything that needs the new version to be live, such as purging a
CDN cache. `ua` sets the User-Agent header. Cloudflare refuses some
library agents. Give `ua` a name of your own.
[`wait_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_http)
verifies HTTPS against the operating system trust store through
`truststore`. A root certificate added there, such as the certificate of
a company proxy, verifies as it does in a browser.
[`wait_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#wait_http)
prints an error message when it differs from the previous one. A wait
that does not succeed shows why.

[`server_health`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#server_health)
reads the state of a server over one SSH call. It returns an `AttrDict`
with these fields. `ram` and `used` are memory in MB. `swap` and
`swap_used` are swap in MB. `pct` is the percentage of RAM in use,
counting swap. `load` is the three load averages as one string. `disk`
is the use of the root disk. `containers` has one line for each
container with its memory and CPU from `docker stats`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vpseasy/blob/main/vpseasy/core.py#L619"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    password:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Return memory and swap in MB, RAM use with swap in percent, the load

### wait_http

``` python
def wait_http(
    url, ua:str='vpseasy', tries:int=40, poll:int=15, timeout:int=10
)->bool:
```

*Ask for `url` until it answers 200, up to `tries` times `poll` seconds
apart, printing each new error, and return whether it did.*

``` python
import http.server, threading
class _H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200 if self.headers['User-Agent'] == 'me' else 403); self.end_headers()
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
_srv = http.server.HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), _H); threading.Thread(target=_srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
_u = f'http://127.0.0.1:{_srv.server_port}/health'
test_eq((wait_http(_u, ua='me', tries=1), wait_http(_u, tries=2, poll=0), wait_http('http://127.0.0.1:9/', tries=1)), (True, False, False))
_srv.shutdown()

import io, ssl, urllib.error, urllib.request
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from unittest import mock
_cert = urllib.error.URLError(ssl.SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate'))
with mock.patch.object(urllib.request, 'urlopen', side_effect=_cert) as _uo, mock.patch.object(time, 'sleep') as _sl:
    with redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()) as _p: test_eq(wait_http('https://e.test/', tries=3, poll=5), False)
test_eq((_uo.call_count, _sl.call_count, _p.getvalue().count('CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED')), (3, 2, 1))
import truststore; test_eq(type(_uo.call_args.kwargs['context']), truststore.SSLContext)

_so = '3820 2410\n4095 512\n0.52 0.40 0.31\n12G/38G (33%)\napp-app-1 1.9GiB / 3GiB 2.1%\ncaddy 40MiB / 256MiB 0.0%'
g = server_health.__globals__; _o = g['run_ssh']; g['run_ssh'] = lambda host, *c, **kw: _so
try: h = server_health('h')
finally: g['run_ssh'] = _o
test_eq((h.ram, h.used, h.swap, h.swap_used, h.pct, h.load, h.disk), (3820, 2410, 4095, 512, 76, '0.52 0.40 0.31', '12G/38G (33%)'))
test_eq(h.containers, ['app-app-1 1.9GiB / 3GiB 2.1%', 'caddy 40MiB / 256MiB 0.0%'])
_w = "\n".join(_so.splitlines()[:4]) + " ;; Warning: Permanently added '1.2.3.4' (ED25519) to the list of known hosts."
g['run_ssh'] = lambda host, *c, **kw: _w
try: h = server_health('h')
finally: g['run_ssh'] = _o
test_eq((h.disk, h.containers), ('12G/38G (33%)', []))
print('wait_http and server_health OK')
```

    wait_http http://127.0.0.1:9/: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>
    wait_http and server_health OK

### Lightsail live test

The next cell creates real AWS resources. It runs only when the
environment variable `VPSEASY_LIVE` has a non-empty value. It creates a
`nano_3_2` instance with
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
user data and no snapshot. It waits for the setup, then checks that the
[`deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#deploy) user
and Docker exist. It creates a bucket and an access key. At the end it
deletes the instance, its static IP and the bucket. Run it with
`VPSEASY_LIVE=1 AWS_PROFILE=<sso profile> uv run nbdev-test --path nbs/00_core.ipynb`.

``` python
if os.environ.get('VPSEASY_LIVE'):
    import secrets
    ln, bn = 'vpseasy-live-test', f'vpseasy-live-test-bkt-{secrets.token_hex(3)}'
    lsl, kp = Lightsail(), gen_key('vpseasy-live-test', key_dir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
    try:
        r = lsl.create(ln, bundle='nano_3_2', cloud_init=vps_init(ln, kp.pub_str), snapshots=None)
        print('instance ip', r.ip)
        wait_ready(r.ip, k=kp.key, tout=600, verbose=True)
        print(run_ssh(r.ip, 'id && docker --version', key=kp.key))
        b = lsl.bucket(bn)
        bk = lsl._c.get_buckets(bucketName=bn)['buckets'][0]
        print('bucket endpoint', b.endpoint, 'reported url', bk['url'], 'location', bk['location'])
    finally:
        lsl.delete(ln)
        with suppress(lsl._c.exceptions.NotFoundException):
            for k in lsl._c.get_bucket_access_keys(bucketName=bn)['accessKeys']:
                lsl._c.delete_bucket_access_key(bucketName=bn, accessKeyId=k['accessKeyId'])
            lsl._c.delete_bucket(bucketName=bn, forceDelete=True)
    test_eq([s for s in lsl.servers() if s['name'] == ln], [])
```

## SSH key helpers

[`load_pub_keys`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#load_pub_keys)
reads public keys from files and returns their text as a list, ready to
pass as `pub_keys` to
[`vps_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vps_init)
or
[`multi_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#multi_init).
With no arguments it reads every `~/.ssh/id_*.pub`. Paths that do not

## Docker Compose helpers

Most small web apps deployed with vpseasy run as the same group of
containers. The `app` container is the app itself. A Caddy container is
the web server in front of it. A `cloudflared` container, usually
present, connects to a Cloudflare tunnel. With the tunnel, the server
needs no open web ports. The containers share a network named `web`.
Caddy keeps its certificates and settings in two named volumes,
`caddy_data` and `caddy_config`.
[`caddy_stack`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#caddy_stack)
writes the Compose file for this group in one call.

[`caddy_stack`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#caddy_stack)
takes the domain and a Dockerfile object from dockeasy, such as
`fasthtml_app()`. It saves `Dockerfile`, `Caddyfile` and
`docker-compose.yml` into `root`, or into the current directory when you
omit `root`. It returns the `Compose` object. `vols` are container
directories whose contents stay on the disk of the server.
[`vols_to_binds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#vols_to_binds)
turns each one into a bind mount from a folder of the same name beside
the Compose file. For example, `/app/data` is stored in `./data`. The
app reads environment variables from `env_file`, which is `.env` by
default. `cloudflared=False` leaves the tunnel out and makes Caddy
listen on ports 80 and 443. `conf` puts the Caddyfile at another path.
Other keyword arguments go to `caddy_svc` from dockeasy, for example
`email=` or `dns=`.

`app_kw`, `caddy_kw` and `cloudflared_kw` add settings to one service
each, such as `mem_limit='3g'` or `init=True`. A `volumes` list in them
is added to the volumes of the service. It does not replace them. For
example, `caddy_kw=dict(volumes=['./static:/srv/static:ro'])` lets Caddy
serve files from the deploy folder. Pass your own dockeasy `Caddyfile`
as `caddyfile` to write it instead of the Caddyfile built from the
options. Pass `write_caddyfile=False` to leave the Caddyfile alone.
Without `conf`, the Caddyfile is in `root` beside the Compose file and
is mounted as `./Caddyfile`. The stack works wherever `root` is. The
next section covers the `litestream` argument.

The
[`caddy_stack`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#caddy_stack)
call without `root` shows the Compose file for a FastHTML app with one
data volume. It saves the files in the current directory.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vpseasy/blob/main/vpseasy/core.py#L642"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Litestream

Litestream copies every change to a SQLite database into an
S3-compatible storage bucket. It can restore the database from that
copy. The bucket can come from
[`Lightsail.bucket`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#lightsail.bucket),
AWS S3 or Cloudflare R2.

[`litestream_conf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#litestream_conf)
writes the Litestream config file and returns its text. `dbs` are
absolute paths inside the container. A relative path raises
`ValueError`. If you pass `vols`, each database must sit inside one of
them. Otherwise
[`litestream_conf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#litestream_conf)
raises `ValueError`, because the Litestream container cannot see the
database. Each database is stored at `<prefix>/<db path>` in the bucket.
Two databases with the same file name do not collide. `region` is `auto`
by default. `snapshot` sets the snapshot interval, `24h` by default.
`retention` sets how long Litestream keeps snapshots, `72h` by default.
The config also sets a validation interval of 12 hours. Litestream reads
the access key from `LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Put both in `.env`. The config format
was tested against `litestream/litestream:0.5` (v0.5.17). Litestream
ignores config keys that it does not recognise, without a warning.

[`litestream_svc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vpseasy/core.html#litestream_svc)
returns the arguments for a Litestream service in `Compose.svc()`. It
mounts the volumes of the app and the config file. It runs `replicate`
unless you pass another command as `cmd`.

You will rarely call either function directly.
`caddy_stack(..., litestream=dict(dbs=..., bucket=..., endpoint=..., region=..., prefix=...))`
writes the config and adds the services. A one-shot `litestream-restore`
service runs `restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists`. That
command restores a database only when the file is missing and a copy
exists in the bucket. The app waits for the restore service to finish
successfully. A fresh server gets its data back before the app can
create an empty database. The long-running `litestream` service starts
after the app. With more than one database, each database has its own
restore service.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vpseasy/blob/main/vpseasy/core.py#L690"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### litestream_svc

``` python
    vols:str='/app/data', conf:str='litestream.yml', env_file:str='.env', image:str='litestream/litestream:0.5',
    cmd:str='replicate', restart:str='unless-stopped', **kw
):
```

*Return `Compose.svc()` arguments for a Litestream container that mounts
the app volumes and the config.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### litestream_conf

``` python
def litestream_conf(
    dbs, bucket, endpoint:NoneType=None, region:str='auto', prefix:NoneType=None, conf:str='litestream.yml',
    retention:str='72h', snapshot:str='24h', vols:NoneType=None
):
```

*Write a Litestream 0.5 config that copies each SQLite database to
`<prefix>/<db path>` in an S3-compatible bucket, and return its text.*

``` python
_d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
y = litestream_conf(['/app/data/palana.db'], 'lh-backups', endpoint='https://s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com',
                    region='ap-southeast-2', prefix='littlehours', conf=_d/'litestream.yml')
assert 'replica:' in y and 'replicas:' not in y
assert 'path: littlehours/app/data/palana.db' in y and 'restore-if-db-not-exists' not in y
y3 = litestream_conf(['/app/data/a.db', '/app/cache/a.db'], 'b', conf=_d/'y3.yml')
assert 'path: app/data/a.db' in y3 and 'path: app/cache/a.db' in y3
assert '${LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID}' in y and '${LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}' in y
test_eq((_d/'litestream.yml').read_text(), y)
y2 = litestream_conf(['/app/data/a.db'], 'b', endpoint='https://acct.r2.cloudflarestorage.com', conf=_d/'l.yml')
assert 'region: auto' in y2 and 'endpoint: https://acct.r2.cloudflarestorage.com' in y2
test_fail(lambda: litestream_conf(['data/a.db'], 'b'), contains='absolute')
test_fail(lambda: litestream_conf(['/tmp/a.db'], 'b', vols=['/app/data'], conf=_d/'x.yml'), contains='/tmp/a.db')
test_fail(lambda: litestream_conf(['/app/database.db'], 'b', vols=['/app/data'], conf=_d/'x.yml'), contains='/app/database.db')

s = litestream_svc()
test_eq(s['image'], 'litestream/litestream:0.5')
test_eq(s['command'], 'replicate')
test_eq(s['volumes'], ['./data:/app/data', './litestream.yml:/etc/litestream.yml'])
test_eq(s['env_file'], ['.env'])
assert 'env_file' not in litestream_svc(env_file=None)
```

``` python
_d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
ls_kw = dict(dbs=['/app/data/palana.db'], bucket='lh-backups', endpoint='https://s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com', region='ap-southeast-2')
c = caddy_stack('lh.example.com', fasthtml_app(), vols=['/app/data'], root=_d, conf=_d/'Caddyfile', litestream=ls_kw)
d = c.to_dict()
svcs = d['services']
assert {'litestream', 'litestream-restore'} <= set(svcs)
test_eq(svcs['app']['depends_on'], {'litestream-restore': {'condition': 'service_completed_successfully'}})
test_eq(svcs['litestream-restore']['command'], 'restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists /app/data/palana.db')
test_eq(svcs['litestream-restore']['restart'], 'no')
test_eq(svcs['litestream']['command'], 'replicate')
test_eq(svcs['litestream']['depends_on'], ['app'])
test_eq(svcs['litestream']['volumes'], ['./data:/app/data', './litestream.yml:/etc/litestream.yml'])
assert (_d/'litestream.yml').exists()
assert "restart: 'no'" in str(c)
d2 = caddy_stack('lh.example.com', fasthtml_app(), vols=['/app/data'], root=_d, conf=_d/'Caddyfile',
                 litestream=ls_kw | dict(dbs=['/app/data/a.db', '/app/data/b.db'])).to_dict()['services']
test_eq(set(d2['app']['depends_on']), {'litestream-restore-app-data-a', 'litestream-restore-app-data-b'})
test_fail(lambda: caddy_stack('lh.example.com', fasthtml_app(), vols=['/app/data'], root=_d, conf=_d/'Caddyfile',
                              litestream=ls_kw | dict(dbs=['/srv/x.db'])), contains='/srv/x.db')
assert 'depends_on' not in caddy_stack('lh.example.com', fasthtml_app(), vols=['/app/data'], root=_d, conf=_d/'Caddyfile').to_dict()['services']['app']
```

### mv_skill_md

``` python
def mv_skill_md(
    dry_run:bool=True, dir:NoneType=None
)->None:
```

*Copy the bundled SKILL.md to `.agents/skills/vpseasy/` and
`~/.claude/skills/vpseasy/`, or only print the targets if `dry_run`.*

``` python
import io, sys, tempfile, os
_d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(_d/'SKILL.md').write_text('test-skill')   # provide a src so function doesn't bail early
_saved_cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(_d)
_buf = io.StringIO(); sys.stdout, _saved = _buf, sys.stdout
mv_skill_md(dry_run=True, dir=str(_d))
sys.stdout = _saved; os.chdir(_saved_cwd)
_out = _buf.getvalue()
assert '.agents/skills/vpseasy/SKILL.md' in _out, _out
assert '.claude/skills/vpseasy/SKILL.md' in _out, _out
print('mv_skill_md dry_run OK')
```
